newsitem.title: RWANDA: Rwanda salutes Kabila victory, recognises new Congo.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda salutes Kabila victory, recognises new Congo.

text.p: Rwanda's government on Monday officially saluted the victory of Laurent Kabila's rebellion in Zaire and hailed the advent of the new Democratic Republic of Congo.

"As the people of the Democratic Republic of Congo celebrate the political change that has occured in their country, the Rwandese government and people would like to express support for this momenteous achievement," said a statement signed by President Pasteur Bizimungu.
"The fall of Kinshasha to the Alliance (of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo) marks a turning point in the history of the people," the statement said.

Rwanda openly backed Kabila's rebel alliance from October last year when it began on the Rwanda/Zaire border. But Kigali has denied providing arms or soldiers to the rebel cause despite the presence of large numbers of troops in eastern Zaire who speak Kinyarwanda, the Rwandese language.
Kabila's forces drew early strength from ethnic Tutsi Banyamulenge tribesman who settled in eastern Zaire from Rwanda about 200 years ago.
While capturing a huge swathe of eastern Zaire last year, the rebels also attacked refugee camps that housed thousands of Hutu extremists who were launching raids in Rwanda.

"The government of Rwanda would like to congratulate and to announce its recognition of the Alliance-led government to be formed by President Laurent Desire Kabila, the new head of state of the Democratic Republic of Congo," said Bizimungu's statement.
